body.statement: The expanded-state transport network has \(2L^2+4L+1\) admissible arcs, and its feasible couplings are in bijection with realized-arm joint distributions induced by laws in \(\mathcal M_L\). The decoder preserves \((s,h)\); unused potential outcomes may be completed arbitrarily.
body.justification: The decoder supplies an independent finite-dimensional sharpness certificate and a destructive check on missing-outcome handling.
body.gap: Generic transportation representations do not identify which network coordinates equal same-layer harm under multilayer missingness.
body.consumer: Auditors of bounds software for protocol-controlled tier assignments obtain a latent-cell program against which the closed form can be tested.
body.proof_tex:
Let
\[
E_z=\begin{cases}
0^{\star},&D_z=0,\\
(D_z,Y_{z,D_z}),&D_z>0.
\end{cases}
\]
Write \(\lambda(0^{\star})=0\) and \(\lambda(d,y)=d\).  Strong tier monotonicity gives \(\lambda(E_0)\le\lambda(E_1)\) almost surely.  There is one arc from \(0^{\star}\) to \(0^{\star}\), there are \(2L\) arcs from \(0^{\star}\) to positive-layer right states, and for each \(1\le i\le j\le L\) there are four outcome-labeled arcs from the two states at layer \(i\) to the two states at layer \(j\).  Therefore the number of admissible arcs is
\[
1+2L+4\sum_{i=1}^{L}(L-i+1)
=1+2L+2L(L+1)
=2L^2+4L+1.
\]

Given a law \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M_L\), assignment overlap states that \(e=P^{\star}(Z=1)\) satisfies \(0<e<1\).  The numbers
\[
\gamma(e_0,e_1)=P^{\star}(E_0=e_0,E_1=e_1)
\]
are supported on precisely those admissible arcs.  Random assignment and the observation map imply that the left and right margins of \(\gamma\) are respectively the observable arm-cell vectors \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\).  Furthermore,
\[
s_d=\sum_{x,y\in\{0,1\}}\gamma((d,x),(d,y)),
\qquad
h_d=\gamma((d,1),(d,0)).
\]
Thus passage to the expanded-state coupling preserves \((s,h)\).

Conversely, let \(\gamma\) be any nonnegative coupling on the admissible arcs with prescribed arm-cell margins.  Draw \((E_0,E_1)\) with law \(\gamma\), set \(D_z=\lambda(E_z)\), and, whenever \(E_z=(d,y)\), set \(Y_{z,d}=y\).  Set every potential outcome not fixed by these realized-arm coordinates equal to zero; any other measurable completion would work as well.  Since every used arc obeys \(\lambda(E_0)\le\lambda(E_1)\), the resulting potential layers satisfy \(D_1\ge D_0\) almost surely.  Finally draw \(Z\) independently of the constructed potential variables, with any assignment probability \(e\in(0,1)\) satisfying assignment overlap; when matching a specified observable law, use its assignment probability.  The observation map then has the prescribed arm-cell margins and the displayed formulas recover the same \((s,h)\).  Hence admissible couplings are in one-to-one correspondence with distributions of the realized-arm pair \((E_0,E_1)\) induced by laws in \(\mathcal M_L\); only the irrelevant completion of unused potential outcomes is nonunique.
